title: Huhum, el sapo que trajo el fuego

jobs.title: Huhum, el sapo que trajo el fuego
jobs.caption: Entrada · contexto
jobs.prompt:
Make a NEW artwork by transforming the supplied own-production paper design references into the specified scene. Image 1 is STYLE ONLY: retain its tactile pure paper-cut construction, not its characters, water wells, or narrative motif. Other reference images identify the required cast/object; do not copy a design-sheet layout. PURE PAPER CUT miniature low-relief diorama photographed straight-on: broad flat hand-cut matte cardstock shapes, rounded near-flat human cutout faces, visible cut edges, small genuine cast shadows BETWEEN paper layers, tangible overlaps. NOT illustration, painting, drawing, CGI faceted polygon heads, folded origami figures, clay people, quilling, rolled paper coils, threads or curly strips. No outer stage base, studio table, display pedestal, border, labels, text or watermark. Low saturation dusty ochre, sand, cream, muted sage/grey-green, desaturated slate blue, soft charcoal; never neon or carnival colors. Leave abundant air, pull camera back, no cropped heads or bodies. Human figures occupy at most 32-40% of image height unless a distant layered world requires smaller. Preserve distinct individual ages and reference facial identity without treating a people as one phenotype. Historical plain ivory unadorned cotton: men plain hip wraps with bare upper torso where reference supports it; women simple rectangular upper piece with flat shoulder straps plus hip wrap. No blue striped modern shirts, spectacular feather headdresses, beads, generic 'tribal' tattoos, Arhuaco pointed caps, Kogi white robes, invented ethnic signs or costume motifs. Only the expressly described festive father in myth357 may have narrated feather attire. Scene is an editorial interpretation, not a claim of authentic ritual iconography.

MYTH 351: Huhum, el sapo que trajo el fuego
PIECE: entrada.
SPECIFIC COMPOSITION: Two Ette adult women place uncooked food on a sun-warmed stone beside their lowland settlement. Far across the Gran Río a tiny enemy-bank hearth has a warm ember. No fire in their own settlement yet.
NARRATIVE GUARDS: Huhum becomes Mamu and REMAINS a toad; no later human return, no fire ritual or enemy combat.
Do not copy the three water wells or Cacica from the style reference. Arrange this particular narrative with a distinct camera staging.

MYTH 351: Huhum, el sapo que trajo el fuego
PIECE: huella.
SPECIFIC COMPOSITION: A single natural squat toad silhouette with one small warm ember just before its mouth, supported by a short blue river-paper strip. Cream negative space. Ember is cut paper, not glowing digital magic.
NARRATIVE GUARDS: Huhum becomes Mamu and REMAINS a toad; no later human return, no fire ritual or enemy combat.
SQUARE SYMBOLIC CLOSING: a single compact meaningful object assemblage on mostly empty warm cream paper, occupying about 45-55% of the canvas. No panoramic scenery, mountains, sky, village, full-body narrative crowd, or repeated action scene. Physically cut low-relief sheets cast shallow natural shadows. Do NOT copy the water-drop symbol from style image1; its semantic motif belongs ONLY to myth352.
